speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you are suffering from neck and arm pain, paresthesias, and muscle weakness; to pinpoint the cause, please describe exactly where the pain radiates and which specific fingers or muscles are affected. Additionally, have you noticed any difficulty with hand coordination or dropping objects?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of burning pain in his neck and arms, accompanying paresthesias in his hands. Over the past 3 months, he has experienced increasing weakness in both hands. He has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and hypertension. He was involved in a motor vehicle accident 3 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Cervical Spondylotic Myelopathy.

Given your long-standing history of burning pain, paresthesias, and progressive bilateral hand weakness alongside your age and vascular risk factors, this strongly suggests cervical spine stenosis compressing the spinal cord. I need to confirm if you have experienced any balance issues, changes in bowel or bladder control, or numbness in your legs, which would further confirm myelopathy. REQUEST IMAGES: Cervical_Spine_MRI.
